rule: Classify the analytic question separately from the source of data and the sex/gender of respondents. Keep patient sex/gender, patient anatomy or indication, and physician sex/gender distinct. Population-specific evidence is not automatically a between-sex comparison. Preserve authors' terminology and measurement details; anatomy, diagnosis, drug use and male/female administrative coding do not establish gender identity. 'Not extracted' marks limits of the current review rather than proof that a variable was absent from the original study.

groups.label: Patient care / access
groups.description: Patient treatment, outcomes, spending or access, including population-specific evidence and qualitative accounts. This group does not imply a male–female comparison.

groups.label: Service / anatomy valuation or coverage
groups.description: Procedure, service or insurer-policy comparisons. Anatomical categories and specialty-level valuation are distinct from measured patient or physician gender.

groups.label: Physician sex / gender
groups.description: Physician sex or gender is the primary comparison in provider payment or service analyses. Results do not directly establish patient-sex disparities.

groups.label: General patient sex / gender background
groups.description: Clinical reviews or commentary addressing sex-related biology and gender-related social pathways, without an original Medicare reimbursement comparison.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Matched CPT-code pairs and fee-schedule years
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Anatomy represented by procedure categories; no patient identity measurement
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Male- versus female-anatomy procedure valuation
studies.inference_boundary: Payment to a physician for a code is not a comparison of physician genders; selected pairs are not all Medicare services.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Matched procedure-code pairs and work/time valuations
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Anatomy represented by procedure categories; no patient identity measurement
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Directly analogous urologic and gynecologic procedures
studies.inference_boundary: Null results in selected pairs do not establish equality across all services or patient access.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Matched procedures, NSQIP patient records and specialty compensation estimates
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Anatomy-specific procedure groups; patient data inform operative resources
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Specialty compensation variable; not physician gender
studies.comparison_axis: Female- versus male-specific procedure work and modeled compensation
studies.inference_boundary: Modeled specialty compensation is not an observed physician-gender effect or a sex-specific Medicare conversion factor.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Surgical registry cases linked to CMS procedure time and RVUs
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Patient clinical case mix; no isolated patient-sex effect extracted
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Surgical specialty comparison; not physician gender
studies.comparison_axis: Valuation and reported versus observed operative time across specialties
studies.inference_boundary: Specialty differences do not isolate either patient-sex or physician-gender discrimination.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Historically matched procedure groups
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Anatomy represented by procedure categories; no patient identity measurement
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Male- versus female-anatomy procedures in the 1995 schedule
studies.inference_boundary: Historical code-payment differences do not measure current coverage or physician-gender pay.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Anatomically matched procedure-code pairs
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Anatomy represented by procedure categories; no patient identity measurement
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Male- versus female-anatomy procedure RVUs and compensation estimates
studies.inference_boundary: Matching assumptions and the underlying FECA source limit direct Medicare interpretation; physician gender is not the extracted comparison.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Breast-reconstruction registry cases and longitudinal code valuations
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Breast-reconstruction indication; no between-sex effect extracted
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Implant versus flap reconstruction and changes over time
studies.inference_boundary: Within-breast-service resource differences do not independently establish patient-sex or physician-gender bias.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Breast procedure types by fee-schedule year and city
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Anatomical service category; no patient cohort
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Breast-procedure payments over time and across locations
studies.inference_boundary: Payment erosion within selected services is not a patient-sex comparison or evidence of physician-gender differences.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Breast-reconstruction patient records grouped by procedure
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Breast-reconstruction indication; no between-sex effect extracted
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Implant, pedicled-flap and free-flap work and payment per time
studies.inference_boundary: Patient records support resource comparisons; no independent sex-disparity estimate is extracted.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Trial participants with provoked vestibulodynia
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Women in an indication-specific trial; not a between-sex contrast
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Physical therapy versus topical lidocaine
studies.inference_boundary: Clinical effectiveness within an eligible population does not establish reimbursement inequity.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Part D drug-product spending, claims, beneficiaries and prescriber data
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Vaginal-estrogen indication; no between-sex effect extracted
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Prescriber data source; no physician-gender effect extracted
studies.comparison_axis: Selected vaginal-estrogen products and spending/utilization over time
studies.inference_boundary: Use of prescriber files does not make this a physician-gender study; product spending is not patient out-of-pocket cost.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Medicare beneficiary records and treatment exposure over time
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Senior women; population restriction rather than between-sex comparison
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Hormone treatment, formulation, route and dose versus nonuse/discontinuation
studies.inference_boundary: Observational treatment-outcome associations do not estimate sex-based reimbursement or prove causal treatment effects.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Randomized trial participants
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Postmenopausal women; population restriction rather than between-sex comparison
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Vaginal estradiol, moisturizer and placebo
studies.inference_boundary: A within-population clinical null result does not determine Medicare coverage or demonstrate reimbursement parity.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Randomized trials synthesized in a systematic review
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Postmenopausal women with GSM; indication-specific evidence
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: GSM treatments versus placebo or alternatives
studies.inference_boundary: Treatment benefit and certainty are clinical evidence; no reimbursement or between-sex effect is extracted.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Randomized trial participants with menopausal symptoms
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Women aged 40–65; indication-specific population
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Fezolinetant versus placebo
studies.inference_boundary: Treatment efficacy is not a coverage comparison; applicability to older Medicare beneficiaries requires assessment.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Participants in two randomized trials
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Postmenopausal women; indication-specific population
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Low-dose paroxetine versus placebo
studies.inference_boundary: Clinical benefit does not establish formulary access or a between-sex disparity.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Published and unpublished randomized trials in a meta-analysis
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Women with HSDD; indication-specific population
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Flibanserin versus placebo
studies.inference_boundary: Benefits and harms within women do not measure physician gender or comparative Medicare reimbursement.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Participants in two randomized trials
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Premenopausal women with HSDD; indication-specific population
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Bremelanotide versus placebo
studies.inference_boundary: Clinical response and adverse effects do not establish sex-based coverage differences.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Randomized trial participants
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Men with hypogonadism and cardiovascular risk; indication-specific population
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Testosterone gel versus placebo
studies.inference_boundary: Male-only safety evidence supplies clinical context, not a matched female comparison or payment-disparity estimate.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Randomized trial participants
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Postmenopausal women with a uterus; sex/anatomy-defined eligibility
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Combined hormone regimen versus placebo for primary prevention
studies.inference_boundary: Regimen-specific benefits and harms do not establish reimbursement differences or apply to every menopausal indication.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Medicare beneficiaries in longitudinal claims
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Recorded patient sex is a direct male–female comparison; identity not established
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: DXA utilization by patient sex and other demographic strata
studies.inference_boundary: Utilization differences do not isolate coverage, clinical need or discrimination.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Male Medicare Advantage beneficiaries assigned to outreach
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Men with fragility fractures; population restriction rather than between-sex comparison
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Physicians receive outreach; no physician-gender effect extracted
studies.comparison_axis: Outreach versus usual care for bone testing and treatment
studies.inference_boundary: Physician participation in an intervention is not physician-gender analysis; no direct female comparator.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Disabled women in claims and coverage transitions
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Women aged 20–49; population restriction rather than between-sex comparison
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Payer/coverage groups and change after dual enrollment
studies.inference_boundary: Coverage-associated contraceptive use is patient-access evidence, not a male–female matched effect.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Reproductive-age beneficiaries in payer-linked claims
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Contraceptive indication/population; no between-sex effect extracted
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Traditional Medicare versus Medicare Advantage and clinical indications
studies.inference_boundary: Payer and method comparisons do not identify patient-sex or physician-gender effects; claims may miss unmet need.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Breast-cancer survivors reporting costs and interviews
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Survivorship population; no matched male–female effect extracted
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Survivors with versus without lymphedema
studies.inference_boundary: Sex/gender identity is not inferred from breast cancer; condition-related costs are not a direct sex-disparity estimate.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Insurers and their published coverage policies
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Condition-specific benefit policies; no patient cohort
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: No physician-level comparison in the extracted policy analysis
studies.comparison_axis: Lymphedema treatment coverage across insurers and modalities
studies.inference_boundary: Published policy is distinct from patient claims, access and sex-specific effects; Medicare applicability needs separate verification.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Ophthalmologists and their Medicare collections
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: No patient-sex disparity estimate extracted
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Physician gender is the primary comparison; measurement details not fully extracted
studies.comparison_axis: Medicare collections by ophthalmologist gender
studies.inference_boundary: Collections are not salary or identical-service payment rates; patient-sex inequity cannot be inferred.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Cardiologists and provider billing/payment measures
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Patient case mix enters adjustment; no patient-sex disparity estimate extracted
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Physician gender is the primary comparison; self-reported gender linked to NPI
studies.comparison_axis: Annual Medicare payments and common-code payments by cardiologist gender
studies.inference_boundary: Provider payments are not salary; adjusted annual differences do not establish unequal rates for identical services.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Part B enrollees, reported utilization and reimbursements
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Enrollment-file sex is a direct male–female comparison; identity not reported
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not extracted as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Beneficiary reimbursement, charges and deductible experience by patient sex
studies.inference_boundary: Payments for physician services are grouped by patient sex here; historical service mix prevents a causal or current-policy inference.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Clinical and preclinical literature in a narrative review
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Sex-related biology and gender-related social influences are general clinical topics
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: No original physician-gender estimate extracted
studies.comparison_axis: General frameworks across diseases and treatments
studies.inference_boundary: Background synthesis supplies rationale; underlying studies require independent screening and cannot be treated as Medicare evidence.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Early-pandemic literature in a narrative review
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Sex/gender-related outcomes and social pathways are general topics
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: No original physician-gender estimate extracted
studies.comparison_axis: Gendered social conditions and early COVID-19 findings
studies.inference_boundary: Narrative background is not an original patient cohort or Medicare reimbursement analysis.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Public-health commentary drawing on earlier research and programs
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Men's care-seeking and gender norms are general access topics
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: No original physician-gender estimate extracted
studies.comparison_axis: Proposed gender-responsive public-health approaches
studies.inference_boundary: Commentary generates access hypotheses; it does not establish Medicare effects or intervention effectiveness.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Nephrologist interviews and qualitative themes
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Patient-sex/gender access barriers are the interview topic; no measured patient cohort
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Clinicians are respondents; no physician-gender disparity estimate extracted
studies.comparison_axis: Clinician perceptions of barriers affecting women's and men's kidney care
studies.inference_boundary: The respondents' profession does not change the patient-access question; perceptions are not measured patient outcomes or Medicare effects.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Surgeons and provider-service payment/utilization measures
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Patient sex is descriptive case mix; no patient-sex disparity estimate extracted
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Physician gender is the primary analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Surgeon gender and provider-service payment/utilization comparisons
studies.inference_boundary: Physician-gender findings do not establish patient-sex reimbursement effects; distinguish provider totals, service rates and salary.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Community-dwelling Medicare beneficiaries in survey-weighted 2016 MCBS analyses
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Enrollment-record sex, female versus male; gender identity not reported and cisgender eligibility unresolved
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not measured as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Patient sex differences in cost-related medication nonadherence and companion financial-burden measures, separately for <65 and >=65
studies.inference_boundary: Adjusted associations are not causal reimbursement effects; historical enrollment sex does not establish cisgender identity. Weighted prevalence does not supply unweighted event counts.

studies.unit_of_analysis: High-hospitalization-risk Medicare beneficiaries with five repeated CRN surveys
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Survey asked sex; authors report woman/man as gender. Gender identity and cisgender eligibility unresolved
studies.physician_sex_gender_role: Not measured as an analytic exposure
studies.comparison_axis: Patient sex differences in transient, intermittent and persistent cost-related medication nonadherence
studies.inference_boundary: Selected observational cohort, not national prevalence or a randomized sex comparison. Adjusted persistent estimate includes null; this does not establish equivalence.

studies.unit_of_analysis: Medicare beneficiary
studies.patient_sex_gender_role: Exact field/source and coding not reported in accessible abstract; claims study population; gender identity not reported

studies.inference_boundary: Shared bone system. Utilization does not identify denied claims or reimbursement causation; identity remains unresolved.

studies.inference_boundary: Shared bone system. Utilization does not identify denied claims or reimbursement causation; identity remains unresolved.
